investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T20:54–21:02Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is consistent across all three checks, indicating the VM-class resource pool is at capacity and no preemption candidates exist. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod stuck unscheduled for 125s.
failed-check.timing: check status=fail, latencyMs=126868, endedAt=2026-07-07T20:57:04.318Z — the pod timed out before reaching a ready state.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the agent pod never started.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 147s — same resource exhaustion pattern on a separate check invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s — confirms the condition persisted across the full eval window (~7 minutes).
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never returned because the pod never scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod did not start.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

[Secondary] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive or nodes were recently re-labeled, effective capacity is reduced even if total cluster capacity appears sufficient.
[Tertiary] Cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have been scaled out to meet concurrent eval or workload demand, causing resource contention.

[Lower confidence] A transient spike in concurrent remote agent workloads (from other users or automated jobs) may have temporarily consumed all VM slots, causing a time-bounded exhaustion that could self-resolve.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is NOT fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and an alternative (e.g., scheduler bug, resource quota, admission webhook rejection) must be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds and produces all four required evidence fields, the exhaustion was transient and self-resolved, suggesting a workload spike rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec is found to match more than 2 nodes (i.e., the 4 'didn't match' nodes are a misconfiguration that has since been corrected), the capacity constraint may be an artifact of label drift rather than true resource exhaustion.

If the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-eligible nodes show available capacity but the pod still fails to schedule, the cause may be a quota, limit range, or admission controller blocking the pod rather than raw resource exhaustion.

If only one of the three sibling checks fails on a subsequent run while the others pass, the failure is not a shared infrastructure condition and a per-check runner or timing issue should be investigated instead.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on eligible nodes and alerts when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.
Add an eval that counts currently running remote agent pods and alerts if the count exceeds an expected baseline, catching slot leakage from incomplete cleanup.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the remote agent scheduling label, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

Consider adding a pre-flight scheduling dryrun eval (e.g., using kubectl --dry-run=server) that validates a remote agent pod would be schedulable before attempting full creation, enabling faster failure detection with a clearer signal.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pods: only 2 nodes carry the kata peer-pods resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval runner never reached the agent-creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was collected and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster (6 nodes total) has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" — reported identically across all three sibling checks — indicates that the 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod VMs have no remaining VM capacity, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. The eval runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers VM provisioning; that provisioning call blocks until the pod is scheduled, times out after ~125–154 seconds, and returns a failure before any evidence fields can be written. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none were produced.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a previous eval run's VMs were not cleaned up, consuming all available VM slots before this eval run started.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, making the effective schedulable pool very small and easily saturated.

Tertiary — VM leak from a prior eval run: if withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903) did not successfully terminate a previous remote agent VM, that leaked VM would hold a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

Lower confidence — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs execute in parallel, the 2 kata-capable nodes may not have enough VM slots to satisfy simultaneous remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T20:54–21:02Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable": 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible by node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is consistent across all three checks, indicating the VM-class resource pool is at capacity and no preemption candidates exist. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returned an agent, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: check status=fail, latencyMs=126868, endedAt=2026-07-07T20:57:04.318Z — the pod timed out before reaching a ready state.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the agent pod never started.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing, matching the contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 147s — same resource exhaustion pattern on a separate check invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck for 144s — confirms the condition persisted across the full eval window (~7 minutes).
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call never returned because the pod never scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod did not start.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption is not possible because no lower-priority victims exist.

[Secondary] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, artificially constraining scheduling to only 2 nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive or nodes were recently re-labeled, effective capacity is reduced even if total cluster capacity appears sufficient.
[Tertiary] Cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have been scaled out to meet concurrent eval or workload demand, causing resource contention.

[Lower confidence] A transient spike in concurrent remote agent workloads (from other users or automated jobs) may have temporarily consumed all VM slots, causing a time-bounded exhaustion that could self-resolve.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of VM slot exhaustion.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature (lines 183-185) failed with the same class of scheduler error, confirming the failure is at the shared pod-creation layer, not in any individual check's logic.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent call for remote agent type
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which submits the pod that the scheduler rejects. No evidence is collected downstream because this call never completes successfully.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to confirm exhaustion and determine how many slots are occupied.

Audit running remote agent pods in the target namespace for any stuck, leaked, or zombie pods that are holding VM slots but should have been terminated — the eval runner uses a withCleanup wrapper (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) which may not have completed cleanup if a prior run was interrupted.

If VM slots are fully consumed by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on those nodes can be increased or whether additional affinity-eligible nodes can be added to the cluster.
Review the node affinity/selector rules applied to remote agent pods to determine whether any of the 4 currently non-matching nodes could be made eligible, expanding the scheduling surface.

Consider adding a pre-flight capacity check to the remote-agent-create eval probe that queries available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots before attempting pod creation, enabling faster and more actionable failure messages.
Monitor whether this failure recurs across subsequent scheduled eval runs to distinguish a transient capacity spike from a persistent exhaustion condition.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of any of the three remote-agents checks with non-empty evidence (orgId, agentId, etc.) would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and has self-resolved.

kubectl describe node output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes would disprove current exhaustion and point instead to a different scheduling constraint.
Scheduler logs showing a different rejection reason (e.g., resource quota, admission webhook, or image pull failure) would shift the root cause away from VM slot exhaustion.

Evidence that the 4 non-matching nodes previously matched the affinity selector and recently lost their labels would shift the primary cause to affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime (which do not use kata.peerpods.io/vm) would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote/kata VM scheduling path and not a broader cluster or API failure.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity eval that queries node allocatable vs. requested VM slots on affinity-eligible nodes and fails with a warning before remote agent pod creation is attempted.
Add a remote-agent-pod-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned remote agent pods remain in the namespace after each eval cycle, catching withCleanup failures that could cause slot leakage.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval for the remote-agents feature that asserts at least N nodes match the required affinity selector, alerting when the eligible node pool shrinks below a safe threshold.

Extend the remote-agent-create check to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler rejection reason as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerMessage, unschedulableReason) so future failures produce actionable evidence rather than an empty evidence object.
